text: The orange-spotted bulbul (Pycnonotus bimaculatus) is a songbird belonging to the bulbul family (Pycnonotidae) within the passerine birds. It is native and found only in Java, Bali, and Sumatra. This species prefers forest edges and open meadows within montane forests. Originally classified in the genus Turdus by Thomas Horsfield in 1821, the Aceh bulbul (Pycnonotus snouckaerti) was previously considered a subspecies of the orange-spotted bulbul until it was split by the International Ornithological Committee (IOC) in 2016; however, most other taxonomic authorities have not yet acknowledged this division. Two subspecies are currently recognized. The bird measures up to 20 cm in length, has a dark coloration, and features a rounded tail. It is highly active and produces a variety of loud, harsh calls and songs. The orange-spotted bulbul is frugivorous and breeds year-round, with nesting activity peaking in May. Its nests are described as robust and cup-shaped. This Pycnonotidae-related article is a stub and can be expanded with additional information on Wikipedia.
